label: Abraham 'Avi' Loeb
narrative: Loeb is what happens when the technical layer refuses to wait for the classified system. Harvard astronomy faculty since 1993, tenured three years later, chair of the astronomy department 2011-2020, Baird Professor since 2012, and director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics since 2007, he founded The Galileo Project on 26 July 2021 - four weeks after the ODNI preliminary assessment - on the explicit premise that the way out of a classified impasse is to build unclassified instruments and publish. The project raised roughly $1.8 million in its first year from donors including Frank Laukien of Bruker and William Linton of Promega, installed its first observatory at Harvard College Observatory in 2022, and published its instrumentation architecture in the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation. In June-July 2023 he led a $1.6 million Pacific Ocean expedition off Papua New Guinea to recover fragments of CNEOS 2014-01-08 (IM1), returning with sub-millimetre spherules that his team classified as a distinct 'BeLaU' composition in Research Notes of the AAS and Chemical Geology. The scientific counter-attack was heavy and specific: Fernando et al. in Geophysical Journal International (March 2024) showed the guiding seismic signal was probably truck traffic; Gallardo argued coal-ash contamination in Research Notes of the AAS; Rudraswami et al. re-evaluated the spherules' origin in Chemical Geology in March 2025. Loeb conceded ground on 3I/ATLAS in 2025-2026 after speculating about its artificiality. Then on 15 June 2026 the position changed entirely: Loeb was named chair of a UAP Science Advisory Council formed at the request of the White House in coordination with AARO, ODNI, the FBI and other agencies - a council with, by contemporaneous reporting, no budget and no access to classified material.
